article_title: Braving the dark: mental health challenges and academic performance of Ukrainian university students during the war.
citation: Pinchuk Irina, Feldman Inna, Seleznova Violetta, Virchenko Volodymyr. (2025). Braving the dark: mental health challenges and academic performance of Ukrainian university students during the war. Social Psychiatry and Psychiatric Epidemiology. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00127-025-02867-7
title: WPAI: SHP questionnaire adapted for academic performance impairment (API) in wartime students
description: The study adapted version 2.0 of the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment: Special Health Problems questionnaire for university students. The authors state that "we replaced the phrase “work productivity” with “academic performance”" and related wording, and extended the recall timeframe from 7 to 14 days based on expert opinion. Answers to Q5 yield the API variable (0–10 self-rated academic performance impairment), and Q2–Q4 yield the HM absenteeism variable used as regression outcomes.
requirements: Respondents must currently be studying at a university; the instrument measures self-rated impairment over the past 14 days, not objective grades
constraints: The authors note the adapted section was answered by 1,398 of 2,364 respondents (59.1%), lowering representativeness relative to the full sample
target_learners: university students (Bachelor's, Master's and PhD) in wartime conditions
target_learning_goals: measuring mental health-related academic performance impairment and study absenteeism
examples: The API variable ranged 0–10 with median 3 (Mean = 3.41, SD = 2.96) in the survey sample
key_sources: Pinchuk Irina, Feldman Inna, Seleznova Violetta, Virchenko Volodymyr. (2025). Braving the dark: mental health challenges and academic performance of Ukrainian university students during the war. Social Psychiatry and Psychiatric Epidemiology. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00127-025-02867-7

article_title: MATLAB codes for teaching quantum physics: Part 1
citation: R. Garcia, A. Zozulya, and J. Stickney. (2007). MATLAB codes for teaching quantum physics: Part 1. https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.1622
title: WPI MATLAB exercise suite for 1D introductory quantum mechanics
description: A set of six MATLAB programs developed at WPI for the first part of a junior-level quantum course based on Griffiths' text, emphasizing "simplicity and quantum pedagogy, not numerical eﬃciency". The exercises show students how to numerically solve 1D problems so as to emphasize the column-vector aspect of kets, the row-vector aspect of bras, and the matrix aspect of operators. Efficient ODE solvers and finite-element techniques are deliberately omitted because they do not serve this purpose.
requirements: The MATLAB programming environment, chosen because its syntax is especially simple for typical matrix operations in 1D quantum problems and because of the ease of plotting functions
constraints: Exercises deliberately omit more efficient ODE solvers and finite-element techniques since they do not serve the pedagogical purpose
A companion Part II on angular momentum and non-commuting observables was only planned, not included
target_learners: undergraduate physics students in a junior-level introductory quantum mechanics course
target_learning_goals: understand that functions correspond to column vectors (kets) and differential operators correspond to matrices in Dirac's formalism
examples: Program 1 plots and numerically integrates trial functions; Program 2 builds derivative and Laplacian matrices; Program 3 solves the infinite square well eigenproblem; Program 4 solves arbitrary potentials with sparse matrices; Program 5 animates double-well probability density; Program 6 propagates wavepackets
key_sources: R. Garcia, A. Zozulya, and J. Stickney. (2007). MATLAB codes for teaching quantum physics: Part 1. https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.1622
